Included ChunkByMut::new with the real Rust body `ChunkByMut { slice, predicate }` so the target call is checked rather than trusted.
Adapted the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` parameter and named return for Verus; the executable target body remains the single call `ChunkByMut::new(slice, pred)`.
Preserved the Rust callback bound `F: FnMut(&T, &T) -> bool`; the harness never invokes the callback in the constructor proof and uses only the audited `fnmut_adjacent_predicate_observed` vocabulary.

Defined the closed iterator-view helper and open adjacent-chunk helper from the extracted mutable initial iterator state to expose old source, remaining, empty yielded prefix/remainder, zero chunk size, forward direction, and predicate-observation lawfulness.

Revealed the closed iterator-view definition in a ghost proof block and added a trigger to the local predicate-observation quantifier; these are proof-only annotations with no executable data-flow effect.
Actual Verus verifies the executable source-backed harness after the repaired generated contract removed the unsound final(slice)@ == old(slice)@ frame.
